claim: The page teaches `ptr := @buffer` to point a ^BYTE pointer and `ptr++` to advance it ('Advance by 1 byte'), `ptr := ptrTable[0] ' Assign to typed pointer`, and notes: "[ptr]++ increments the VALUE at ptr; ptr++ advances the POINTER itself". The v55 pointer table says the reverse: `ptrvar` alone is the pointed-to variable, `[ptrvar]` is the pointer itself, `[ptrvar] := @regvar` points it, `[ptrvar]++` steps it. The same page's gotcha (and STRUCT.yaml's) already uses `[pCfg] := sensor.getConfig()` to set a pointer, and without the brackets the compiler rejects it (scratch t/v4_parent_bracket vs t/v5_parent_nobracket). Every example above compiles (except the ^point one, a registered class), so the gate cannot see it; registered as defects class `typed-pointer-assignment-and-increment` (claim sites).

claim: FILE is described as a 'Compiler directive for file inclusion' with syntax `FILE filename` and the example `FILE "config.spin2"`. FILE is a DAT data directive (`FileDat FILE "Filename"`) that includes a BINARY file's bytes at that point of a DAT block; it is not allowed in inline PASM, and source inclusion is the preprocessor's #INCLUDE. The block compiles in DAT with an existing file (gate decision: fragment/pasm2-dat, assumes file:config.spin2), so the gate cannot see the description.

claim: at.yaml: 'In Spin2+PASM programs: @ returns an address RELATIVE to the start of the object' and 'In Spin2+PASM, @ addresses are object-relative, not absolute'. double_at.yaml: "@ in PUB/PRI code is already resolved", "Direct @ in code is already absolute; @@ is for stored offsets". The two pages cannot both hold for `addr := @mydata` in a method; at.yaml's own example then hands such an @ to COGINIT(COGEXEC_NEW, @asm_code, 0). Which one is right is undetermined here (v55 states the relative rule for 'symbols that precede data', :297-301, and the stored-offset rule for @@, :300; it does not say what a bare @ in PUB code yields).

memory_spaces.cog_registers.sections gives '$120-$13F: Reserved', '$140-$1CF: LUT access window', '$1D0-$1D7: Special hardware registers', '$000-$11F: General purpose / user code space'. The v55 inline-PASM section lists: $000..$11F user load area, $1D8..$1DF PR0..PR7, $1E0..$1EF the method's first 16 longs, $1F0..$1FF IJMP3..INB, and says to avoid writing $120..$1D7 because the Spin2 interpreter occupies it. There is no 'LUT access window' inside cog RAM (LUT is a separate $200-$3FF space, which the page lists correctly two lines later), and `$1D0-$1D7` is not named in the source.

ADDBITS is described as 'Add bit count to pin number' (category Pin) with `pin_range := start_pin ADDBITS bit_count`. ADDBITS makes a BITFIELD value: (x & $1F) | (y & $1F) << 5 (ADDPINS is the pinfield twin, << 6). It adds nothing and is not a pin operator; ADDPINS is the pin one.

operation.description says 'Performs (value % modulus) where % is unsigned modulo ... Equivalent to: value // modulus'. The file's own header (lines 1-12) and v55 define `//` as the SIGNED remainder and `+//` as the unsigned one, so `value // modulus` is not equivalent for operands with bit 31 set.

Level 2 lists `NOT` beside `!`, while the page's own note (:84) and v55 put the logical `!!`/`NOT` at priority 12. The ternary is described 'PUB/PRI only' (:64, :86); v55's operator table heads the ternary row 'Term (All blocks)' (priority 16), i.e. usable in CON/DAT expressions too. (S-057 already covers the same family in operators.yaml; the operator ingestion proper is «#402».)

precedence is `level: 6` with `same_level: "+, -, +., -."`. Those operators are priority 8 (6 is `|`). Compiled probes show POW groups left-to-right at the SAME level as `+`/`-`/`-.` (`a -. b POW c` == `(a -. b) POW c`, `a POW b -. c` == `(a POW b) -. c`), tighter than `#>`/comparisons/`&&`/`||`, and looser than `|` and `*.` (`a | b POW c` == `(a | b) POW c`): the 'same level' is right, the number 6 is wrong (8). precedence.yaml carries no POW row at all.
